subject: Climate & Environment
title: The Paris Agreement
description: A quick, practical guide to The Paris Agreement.

hook.text: In 2015, 196 countries promised to keep warming well below 2°C, aiming for 1.5°C.

buildup.text: Each nation set its own target. There are no penalties for missing them.

discovery.text: The deal relies on peer pressure and transparency — countries report progress publicly.

twist.text: Current pledges put the world on track for about 2.5 to 2.8°C of warming.

climax.text: The gap between promises and action is the biggest challenge in climate politics.

punchline.text: The world signed a deal. Now it needs to keep it.

quiz.question: What temperature target does the Paris Agreement set?

details.summary: The Paris Agreement, adopted in 2015 by 196 parties, commits nations to limit warming to well below 2 degrees and pursue 1.5 degrees. Countries submit voluntary emission reduction pledges called Nationally Determined Contributions, updated every five years.
details.whyItMatters: The Paris Agreement is the first universal climate treaty. Its success depends on whether countries turn voluntary pledges into enforceable domestic policy and increase ambition over time.
takeaways: 196 parties adopted the agreement in December 2015
NDCs are voluntary pledges updated every five years
Current pledges collectively fall far short of the 1.5-degree target

faq.question: Are countries meeting their Paris Agreement pledges?
faq.answer: As of 2024, most major emitters are not on track to meet their own NDC targets. Even if all current pledges were fully implemented, the world would warm roughly 2.5 to 2.8 degrees by 2100, well above the 1.5-degree goal.

faq.question: What happens if a country withdraws from the Paris Agreement?
faq.answer: There is no enforcement mechanism. The US withdrew under President Trump in 2020 and rejoined under President Biden in 2021. The voluntary structure makes the agreement flexible but limits its ability to compel action.
